messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@signet.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-11-29T14:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing probe — initial telemetry attached

Neha —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is a 72-hour anonymized sample of our request telemetry (signet_sample_telemetry_3d.csv). High-level summary so you can start sizing:

- Typical sustained QPS: ~350 req/s; expected monthly growth ~15%.
- Peak sustained window (daily): ~1,200 concurrent sessions during regional business hours (US east coast).
- Prompt characteristics: median prompt length ~40 tokens, 95th percentile ~400 tokens.
- Response characteristics: median response ~180 tokens, mean ~220 tokens, 95th percentile ~1,200 tokens (long form).
- Multi-turn sessions: ~15% of sessions are multi-turn, avg turns ~6, context retention required across turns (we send full context).
- KV/Prefix reuse: we observe ~35% reuse of repeated prefixes across sessions (hot prompts).
- Service composition: ~20% of calls use function-calling or structured JSON output. Embeddings are handled separately (<5% of volume).
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms, p99 target < 350ms for user-facing features; background tasks can tolerate ~1s.
- Preferred GPU baseline: we are leaning toward H100 inference instances but open to A100 sizing guidance for cost comparisons.
- Objective: size a reserved capacity commitment for a 3-month pilot (with burst to on-demand) and a recommended steady-state reserved count if we commit 12 months.

Can you provide a quick sketch of the fleet we should reserve (GPU counts by SKU), recommended bursting headroom, and any urgent telemetry artifacts you need beyond the CSV? Also propose a time for a 30-minute call with your sizing folks (we prefer US morning).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Head of Platform | Signet.ai

Attachment: signet_sample_telemetry_3d.csv (CSV, 3 days anonymized request logs)

From: neha_kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Rajiv —

Appreciate the CSV and the crisp summary. We can definitely put together a pilot sizing + reserved/ burst recommendation. Quick clarifying questions (short answers will speed the sketch):

1) Burst shape: when you say "burst to on-demand," is your expected burst multiplier 2x–3x of peak for occasional events, or do you need headroom for sustained 6–12 hour regional spikes?
2) Hard vs soft latency: you gave p99 target <350ms — is that a hard SLA for all user-facing calls or only for the subset flagged as "interactive"? Rough split of interactive vs background calls helps.
3) Session affinity: do you require strict KV-cache pinning to the same GPU (session stickiness) for correctness, or can we use shuffled KV cache with best-effort affinity?
4) Model family / tokenizer: which model(s) will you run in prod (family name and approximate param size)? This changes memory and KV cache sizing a lot.
5) Off-peak CPU/async handling: do you have a backlog window where longer responses (the 95th/long-form outputs) can be async?

Immediate items we can produce after your answers:
- Pilot reserved SKU sketch (H100 vs A100 cost/latency tradeoffs), per-GPU expected sustained throughput and p95/p99 projections based on your token mix.
- Recommended burst policy (headroom + guardrails) and fallback variant suggestions.
- A compact runbook of telemetry fields we need to auto-validate viability for a reserved commit (sample schema included).

Propose a 30-minute call tomorrow (US EST) at 10:30am — Karthik (infrastructure sizing) and Marissa (cost & pricing) will join. If another time works, tell me.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Neha — quick answers inline:

> 1) Burst shape: when you say \"burst to on-demand,\" is your expected burst multiplier 2x–3x of peak ...
We expect short bursts up to ~2.5x peak for traffic storms (minutes to an hour) and occaisional prolonged spikes (2–6 hours) around product launches. The 2.5x figure is our design goal.

> 2) Hard vs soft latency: you gave p99 target <350ms — is that a hard SLA ...
Interactive subset = ~70% of user-facing calls; those need the tighter p95/p99. Background jobs (20% of total) can be 500–1000ms.

> 3) Session affinity: do you require strict KV-cache pinning ...
We prefer strong affinity for better cache hits; current implementation assumes session stickiness but we can tolerate best-effort for some endpoints.

> 4) Model family / tokenizer: which model(s) will you run in prod ...
Primary: signet-13B (optimized variant, 13B) and signet-70B for long-form summaries. We'll likely route shorter requests to 13B and long responses to 70B. Tokenizer is standard bpe-like with UTF-8; we can share tokenizer stats if needed.

> 5) Off-peak CPU/async handling: do you have a backlog window ...
Yes — ~10% of the long-form responses are okay to be async and batched during off-peak windows.

Also added a Drive link with a slightly larger anonymized dump (same folder as the CSV). Happy to do the call at 10:30am EST tomorrow.

—Rajiv
